questions.question: Which mapped type removes `readonly` from every property of T?
questions.explanation: A - prefix removes a modifier. -readonly removes readonly; -? removes the optional modifier. The first option adds readonly.

questions.question: Given `type Fund = { readonly code: string; navInr?: number }`, what does `{ [P in "code" | "navInr"]: Fund[P] }` produce?
options: An error, because P must extend keyof T
questions.explanation: Mapping over a plain literal union is not homomorphic, so readonly and ? are not copied. The property types are read through Fund[P], so navInr keeps undefined in its type but becomes required.

questions.question: In a mapped type, what happens to a key whose `as` clause evaluates to `never`?
options: The key is removed from the resulting type
questions.explanation: Remapping a key to never filters it out. This is how you build types like PickByValue or an Omit that works on any condition.

questions.question: In a getter-generating mapped type, why is the key written as `Capitalize<string & K>` instead of `Capitalize<K>`?
options: Because K is always a number
Because keyof T may include number and symbol keys, and Capitalize only accepts string types
Because template literal types require intersections
Because it makes the getter methods optional
questions.explanation: keyof T is string | number | symbol in general. Intersecting with string keeps only string keys, which is what Capitalize and template literals need.
